I Assent

ERROL CHARLES,

March 27, 2025.
SAINT LUCIA
_________
No. 5 of 2025
AN ACT to provide for the establishment of the Sovereign
Wealth Fund of Saint Lucia and for related matters.
[ 31st March, 2025 ]
BE IT ENACTED by the King’s Most Excellent Majesty, by
and with the advice and consent of the House of Assembly and Senate
of Saint Lucia, and by the authority of the same, as follows:

50
No. 5 ] Sovereign Wealth Fund of Saint Lucia Act [ 2025
PRELIMINARY
Short title and commencement
1.—(1) This Act may be cited as the Sovereign Wealth Fund of
Saint Lucia Saint Lucia Act, 2025.
(2) This Act shall come into force on a date to be fixed by the
Minister by Order published in the Gazette.
Interpretation
2. In this Act —
“Appropriation Act” —
(a) means an Act which authorizes the application of a sum
out of the Fund for the purpose of the Fund;
(b) includes a Supplementary Appropriation Act;
“asset” means —
(a) real or personal property;
(b) a part or share of an asset or interest in an asset;
“Board” means the Sovereign Wealth Fund of Saint Lucia
Board established under section 5;
“Chairperson” means the Chairperson designated under
section 7;
“climate change” means a change of climate which is
attributed directly or indirectly to human activity that
alters the composition of the global atmosphere and which
is in addition to natural climate variability observed over
comparable time periods, the effects of which can be
altered by climate change mitigation and climate change
adaptation measures;
“climate change adaptation” means the initiatives and measures
to reduce the vulnerability of natural and human systems
to actual or expected climate change effects;

51
No. 5 ] Sovereign Wealth Fund of Saint Lucia Act [ 2025
“Climate Change Adaptation Policy” means the Climate
Change Adaptation Policy under section 18 of the Climate
Change Act, No. 3 of 2024;
“climate change mitigation” means technological change and
substitution that reduces resource inputs and emissions per
unit of output;
“Corporate Secretary” means the Corporate Secretary
appointed under section 24;
“custodian” means the custodian appointed under section 33;
“financial year” has the meaning assigned under section 2 of
the Public Finance Management Act, Cap. 15.05;
“Fund”—
(a) means the Sovereign Wealth Fund of Saint Lucia
established under section 3; and
(b) in relation to anything said to be done by the Fund,
means the Board or an agent or employee of the Board
acting on the authority of the Board;
“Investment Manager” means the Investment Manager
appointed under section 34;
“member” means the Chairperson or a member of the Board
appointed under section 6;
“Minister” means the Minister responsible for finance;
“risk-adjusted return” means a return based on an objective
measurement of how much risk is involved in producing
that return.
PART I
SOVEREIGN WEALTH FUND OF SAINT LUCIA
Establishment of Sovereign Wealth Fund of Saint Lucia
3.—(1) There is established a Fund, to be known as the Sovereign
Wealth Fund of Saint Lucia.
(2) The Fund is a public fund.

52
No. 5 ] Sovereign Wealth Fund of Saint Lucia Act [ 2025
Purpose of the Fund
4.—(1) The purpose of the Fund is to support investments in climate
adaptation, climate mitigation and sustainable economic development.
(2) Without limiting the generality of subsection (1), the purpose
of the Fund is to —
(a) increase savings to build national resilience in accordance
with the Climate Change Adaptation Policy;
(b) fund social and economic development in accordance with
the Climate Change Adaptation Policy.
PART II
MANAGEMENT OF THE FUND
Division 1
Sovereign Wealth Fund of Saint Lucia Board
Establishment of Sovereign Wealth Fund of Saint Lucia Board
5.—(1) There is established the Sovereign Wealth Fund of Saint
Lucia Board.
(2) The Board is a body corporate to which section 19 of the
Interpretation Act, Cap. 1.06 applies.
Composition of the Board
6.—(1) The Board consists of —
(a) the Corporate Secretary, who shall be an ex officio
member of the Board; and
(b) nine members appointed, subject to subsection (2), by
the Minister, with the approval of Cabinet.
(2) A person is qualified for appointment as a member of the
Board if the person has one or more of the following —
(a) holds a degree in economics, finance, accounting, law or
other relevant degree from an accredited university;
(b) has over five years experience at senior management level
in the field of management of investment portfolios;

53
No. 5 ] Sovereign Wealth Fund of Saint Lucia Act [ 2025
(c) has over ten years post-qualification professional experience
in matters relating to law, financial management or venture
capital fund management.
(3) The Minister shall, by Notice published in the Gazette,
provide the names of the members of the Board as first constituted
and every change in the constitution of the Board.
Designation of the Chairperson and Deputy Chairperson
7.—(1) The Minister shall, subject to subsection (2), designate one
member of the Board as the Chairperson of the Board and another
member as Deputy Chairperson of the Board.
(2) A member is qualified for designation as the Chairperson or
Deputy Chairperson if the member has one or more of the following —
(a) holds a minimum of a degree from an accredited university;
(b) has experience in a senior management position in the
private sector;
(c) holds at least ten years relevant post-qualification
professional experience;
(d) is a member of a professional body.
(3) Where the Chairperson is absent, the Deputy Chairperson
has all the powers of the Chairperson.
Disqualification
8.—(1) A person shall not be qualified to be appointed or hold
office as a member if —
(a) he or she, or his or her spouse is a director of or is
in the full-time employment of an entity in which the
Fund has made an investment;
(b) he or she has been adjudged or otherwise declared
insolvent or bankrupt in terms of a law in force in any
country, and has not been rehabilitated or discharged;
(c) he or she has made an assignment to or arrangement
or composition with his or her creditors in terms of
a law in force in any country, and the assignment,

54
No. 5 ] Sovereign Wealth Fund of Saint Lucia Act [ 2025
arrangement or composition has not been rescinded or
set aside;
(d) within the period of five years immediately preceding
his or her proposed appointment, he or she has been
sentenced—
(i) in Saint Lucia, in respect of an offence except where
the offence is a minor traffic offence or has been
spent under the Criminal Records (Rehabilitation
of Offenders) Act, Cap. 3.13, or
(ii) outside Saint Lucia, in respect of conduct which, if
committed in Saint Lucia, would have constituted
an offence,
to a term of imprisonment of not less than six months
imposed without the option of a fine, whether or not
any portion has been suspended, and has not received
a free pardon;
(e) he or she has been convicted —
(i) in Saint Lucia, of an offence involving dishonesty,
or
(ii) outside Saint Lucia, in respect of any conduct
which, if committed in Saint Lucia, would have
constituted an offence involving dishonesty; and
sentenced to a fine of any amount or to a term of
imprisonment of any duration, whether or not any part
of the sentence has been suspended; or
(f) he or she is a member of Parliament;
(g) he or she is a public officer or other employee of the
Government.
(2) A person shall not, knowing that he or she is disqualified
under this section to hold office as a member —
(a) attend a meeting of the Board as a member; or
(b) perform any other act as a member.

55
No. 5 ] Sovereign Wealth Fund of Saint Lucia Act [ 2025
(3) A person who contravenes subsection (2) commits an
offence and is liable to a fine not exceeding five thousand dollars or
to imprisonment for a period not exceeding six months or to both fine
and imprisonment.
Functions of the Board
9.—(1) The function of the Board is to administer the Fund.
(2) Without limiting the generality of subsection (1), the functions
of the Board are —
(a) to oversee the investment and management of the Fund
in accordance with this Act;
(b) to determine the investment guidelines, including the
rules, policies and directions that are most appropriate in
relation to moneys standing to the credit of the Fund in
accordance with the investment mandate approved by the
Minister under paragraph (d);
(c) to appoint, with the approval of the Minister and Cabinet,
the custodian and Investment Managers;
(d) to prepare and review periodically a written investment
mandate on or before such date as the Minister and the
Board agree and submit the investment mandate for the
approval of the Minister;
(e) to make reports, such as the quarterly report available to
the public including on a website;
(f) to attract co-investment from other investors, including
strategic investors, sovereign and internationally
recognized investment funds and private companies;
(g) to develop the criteria for selecting investments in climate
adaptation, climate mitigation and sustainable economic
development;
(h) to carry out other activities as may be related to the
functions under paragraphs (a) to (g).

56
No. 5 ] Sovereign Wealth Fund of Saint Lucia Act [ 2025
(3) A written investment mandate under subsection (2)(d) must
include —
(a) classes of investment the Fund will make and the selection
criteria for each of the classes for local and foreign
investments;
(b) benchmarks and standards against which the performance
of asset classes and the Fund as a whole will be compared;
(c) standards for reporting the investment performance of the
Fund;
(d) ethical and responsible investment requirements, including
any requirement for environmental and decarbonisation
impact, and anti-bribery and corruption diligence and
protection;
(e) the balance between risk and return in the overall portfolio;
(f) the fund management structure;
(g) the governance framework for the implementation and
operation of fund investment vehicles established for the
purposes of holding, facilitating or managing specific
Fund investments;
(h) the use of options, futures and other derivative financial
instruments;
(i) the management of credit, liquidity, currency and other
financial risks;
(j) the retention, exercise or delegation of voting rights
acquired through investments;
(k) the method of, and basis for valuation of, investments that
are not regularly traded at a public exchange; and
(l) prohibited or restricted investments, and any constraints
or limits on particular investments.
(4) The criteria developed under subsection (2)(g) must be
communicated to the Minister.

57
No. 5 ] Sovereign Wealth Fund of Saint Lucia Act [ 2025
Powers of the Board
10.—(1) The Board has the powers necessary for the proper
performance of its functions under this Act.
(2) Without limiting the generality of subsection (1), the Board
has power to —
(a) enter into contracts;
(b) open a bank account for the Fund into which moneys
received by or on behalf of the Fund is paid in the first
instance and out of which all payments made by the Fund
is made;
(c) undertake any activity necessary for the fulfillment of the
objects of the Fund under this Act.
Delegation of functions or powers
11. The Board may, by resolution of a majority of its members,
for the purpose of carrying out its functions under this Act, delegate,in
writing to one or more of its members, a function or power specified
under section 9 or 10 that the Board is authorized to exercise or
perform under this Act.
Committees of the Board
12.—(1) Without prejudice to section 11, the Board may appoint a
committee to carry out a functions or power of the Board.
(2) Notwithstanding subsection (1), the Board may appoint —
(a) an Audit Committee;
(b) an Appointments Committee to make recommendations
to the Board on the suitability of persons to be employed
or retained by the Board;
(c) an Investments Committee to monitor the investments of
the Fund;
(d) a Discipline and Ethics Committee to monitor and enforce
compliance with the code of conduct and ethics of the
Board; and

58
No. 5 ] Sovereign Wealth Fund of Saint Lucia Act [ 2025
(e) a Risk Management Committee to assess, monitor and
manage specific and overall risks affecting the Fund.
(3) A committee appointed under this section shall regulate its
proceedings after consultation with the Board.
Term of appointment
13.—(1) Subject to subsection (2), the Board is appointed for a
term not exceeding five years with —
(a) three members appointed for five years;
(b) three members appointed for four years;
(c) three members appointed for three years.
(2) A member of the Board is eligible for reappointment for not
more than one term.
Leave of absence
14. The Minister may, on the application of a member of the
Board in writing, grant leave of absence to the member for a period
not exceeding three months.
Resignation
15.—(1) A member of the Board other than the Chairperson,
may, by written notice addressed to the Minister and through the
Chairperson, resign from his or her office.
(2) The Chairperson may, by written notice addressed to the
Minister, resign from his or her office.
Suspension of member
16.—(1) The Minister —
(a) may suspend from office a member against whom
criminal proceedings are instituted for an offence
involving dishonesty;
(b) may suspend a member from office if there are
reasonable grounds to believe that the member’s office
has become vacant but the member has not relinquished
office;

59
No. 5 ] Sovereign Wealth Fund of Saint Lucia Act [ 2025
(c) shall suspend a member from office if there are
reasonable grounds for suspecting that the member is
disqualified;
pending determination of the question whether the member is to vacate
his or her office.
(2) A member who is suspended under subsection (1) shall not
carry out any duties or be entitled to any remuneration or allowances
as a member during the suspension.
Revocation
17. The Minister may, by written notice, revoke the appointment
of a member of the Board if the Minister is satisfied that the member —
(a) is disqualified from being a member of the Board under
section 8;
(b) is unable to perform the functions of his or her office;
(c) commits an act of misconduct under section 23(4); or
(d) has contravened section 36(2);
(e) has failed to attend three consecutive meetings of the Board
without presenting a medical certificate or without being
excused —
(i) in the case of the Chairperson, by the Minister in
writing, or
(ii) in the case of any other member, by the Chairperson
in writing.
Vacancy
18.—(1) The office of a member of the Board is vacated —
(a) on the death of the member;
(b) if the member becomes disqualified under section 8;
(c) if the member resigns under section 15;
(d) if the Minister revokes the appointment of the member
under section 17; or
(e) on the expiry of the member’s term of appointment.

60
No. 5 ] Sovereign Wealth Fund of Saint Lucia Act [ 2025
(2) A decision of the Board taken at a meeting is not invalidated
by a vacancy in the membership as long as there is the quorum required
under section 22.
Temporary appointment
19.—(1) The Minister may appoint a person to act temporarily in
place of a member of the Board who —
(a) has been granted a leave of absence under section 14;
or
(b) is unable to perform the functions of his or her office.
(2) A person appointed under subsection (1) shall act —
(a) for the duration of the absence or inability of the member
of the Board; or
(b) until another person is appointed in accordance with
section 6.
Meetings
20.—(1) The Board shall meet at least quarterly or at times as may
be necessary or expedient for the transaction of business of the Board.
(2) The meetings of the Board must be held at the day and time
the Chairperson determines.
(3) The Chairperson may call a special meeting of the Board
within forty-eight hours of receipt of a written request for that purpose
addressed to the Chairperson by three members of the Board or the
Minister.
(4) The Chairperson and any other member of the Board is
deemed to be present at a meeting of the Board if the Chairperson or
the other members of the Board participates by telephone, video link
or satellite, and all members of the Board participating in the meeting
are able to hear and speak to each other.
(5) At a meeting of the Board —
(a) the Chairperson shall preside;
(b) if the Chairperson is not present, the Deputy Chairperson
shall preside; or

61
No. 5 ] Sovereign Wealth Fund of Saint Lucia Act [ 2025
(c) if the Chairperson or the Deputy Chairperson is not
present, the members present shall choose one of their
number to preside.
Co-opting
21.—(1) Subject to subsection (2), the Board may co-opt a person
to attend a meeting of the Board at which it is proposed to deal with a
particular matter, for the purpose of assisting or advising the Board.
(2) A co-opted member of the Board does not have the right to
vote.
Quorum
22. A meeting of the Board is constituted if at the meeting there
is the presence of the Chairperson or Deputy Chairperson or the
member chosen to preside under section 22(5)(c) and a quorum of
not less than two-thirds of the members participating in the meeting.
Declaration of interest and abstention from voting
23.—(1) A member of the Board who has a pecuniary or other
interest in a matter before the Board shall declare the nature of his or
her interest at the first meeting of the Board at which it is practicable
to do so.
(2) Where a member of the Board declares an interest under
subsection (1), the member of the Board shall leave the meeting
on the matter coming up for discussion and shall not receive other
communication on the matter.
(3) A declaration under subsection (1) and the departure of a
member of the Board from the meeting under subsection (2) must be
noted in the minutes of the meeting.
(4) A member of the Board commits an act of misconduct if he
or she —
(a) contravenes subsection (1);
(b) votes in respect of a matter before the Board in which he
or she has an interest; or
(c) seeks to influence the vote of another member of the Board
in relation to a matter before the Board.

62
No. 5 ] Sovereign Wealth Fund of Saint Lucia Act [ 2025
(5) Where a person contravenes subsection (1), his or her
appointment may be revoked under section 17(c).
Corporate Secretary
24.—(1) The Board shall appoint, on the advice of the Minister,
a person to be the Corporate Secretary to the Board.
(2) A person is qualified to be appointed under subsection (1)
if he or she —
(a) holds a bachelors degree in law from an accredited
university;
(b) has at least ten years experience in management of
investment portfolios, business administration or
management, economics, accounts, law or finance.
(3) The Corporate Secretary shall —
(a) record the minutes of each meeting of the Board;
(b) keep the minutes in a safe place;
(c) produce the minutes at the next meeting of the Board to
be confirmed by the Board;
(d) submit the minutes of the meeting for signing by the
Chairperson or Deputy Chairperson or the member chosen
to preside under section 22(5)(c);
(e) implement the decisions of the Board;
(f) measure and attain performance targets approved by the
Board;
(g) communicate decisions of the Board, policies and priorities
to the custodian and Investment Managers;
(h) present organizational performance reports and estimates
of revenue and expenditure to the Board;
(i) vet payments from the Fund in accordance with section
46; and
(j) perform the functions assigned to him or her by the
Minister and under this Act.

63
No. 5 ] Sovereign Wealth Fund of Saint Lucia Act [ 2025
(4) In the absence of the Corporate Secretary, the Board may,
on the advice of the Minister, appoint a person to act as the Corporate
Secretary in accordance with subsection (2).
Decisions of the Board
25.—(1) Decisions of the Board shall be taken by a simple majority
of votes of directors present and voting at the meeting.
(2) The Chairperson has an original vote and in cases of equal
division the Chairperson has the casting vote.
(3) In the absence of the Chairperson and in the case of an equal
division of votes, the Deputy Chairperson has the casting vote.
(4) In the absence of the Chairperson and the Deputy Chairperson
and in the case of an equal division of votes, the member chosen to
preside under section 22(5)(c) has the casting vote.
Seal
26.—(1) The Board shall have an official seal.
(2) The affixing of the official seal of the Board shall be in the
presence of, and witnessed by —
(a) the Chairperson or the Deputy Chairperson; and
(b) the Corporate Secretary.
Signification of other documents
27. A document, other than a document required by law to be
under seal, which is executed by, and a decision of, the Board shall
be signed by —
(a) the Chairperson or a member of the Board who is
authorized in writing by the Chairperson to act on behalf
of the Chairperson; and
(b) the Corporate Secretary.
Service of documents
28. The service of documents on the Board is effective if delivered
at the prescribed place.

64
No. 5 ] Sovereign Wealth Fund of Saint Lucia Act [ 2025
Board to regulate its own procedures
29. Subject to this Act, the Board shall regulate its own
procedures.
Remuneration
30. A member of the Board shall be paid remuneration as
determined by Cabinet.
Directions from the Minister
31.—(1) Subject to subsection (2), the Minister shall, in consultation
with the Chairperson, give to the Board directions of a general
character as to the policy to be followed in the performance of its
functions in relation to matters appearing to him or her to concern
the public interest.
(2) A direction under subsection (1) must not be given to —
(a) invest an amount from the Fund in a particular asset;
(b) allocate assets to —
(i) a particular business entity, or
(ii) a particular activity.
(3) The Board shall furnish the Minister with such returns,
accounts and other information as he or she may require with respect
to the functions of the Board, and shall afford him or her facilities for
verifying such information in such manner and at such times as he or
she may reasonably require.
(4) The Board shall comply with the policy directions under
subsection (1).
Exemption from taxes and duties
32. Notwithstanding any other law, the Board is exempt from
the payment of taxes and duties.

65
No. 5 ] Sovereign Wealth Fund of Saint Lucia Act [ 2025
Division 2
Appointment of the Custodian and Investment Managers
Custodian
33.—(1) The Board shall, on the advice of the Minister and Cabinet,
appoint, by instrument in writing on terms and conditions the Board,
on the advice of the Minister and Cabinet determines, a custodian
for the Fund.
(2) A custodian appointed under subsection (1) holds the property
of the Fund in his or her name or if the Board authorizes, in the name
of one or more nominees.
Investment Manager
34.—(1) Subject to subsection (2), the Board shall, on the advice
of the Minister, appoint one or more Investment Managers as may be
necessary for the proper discharge of its functions.
(2) The Board may appoint an Investment Manager under
subsection (1) if the Board is satisfied that the Investment Manager —
(a) meets the minimum technical qualifications;
(b) is a body corporate with sufficient equity capital, adequate
risk management and internal control systems as well as
sufficient guarantees and insurance against operational
risks;
(c) has a sound record of operational and financial performance;
(d) has the highest standards of experience, knowledge and
reputation in fund management;
(e) has a good track record of managing large investment
portfolios of equivalent or high magnitudes;
(f) is able to provide such information and reports at such
times and in such a manner as the Board determines;
(g) meets other condition as the Board specifies.
(3) An Investment Manager shall be appointed under subsection
(1), by instrument in writing on terms and conditions the Board
determines and after consultation with the Minister.

66
No. 5 ] Sovereign Wealth Fund of Saint Lucia Act [ 2025
Functions of Investment Manager
35.—(1) The functions of an Investment Manager are —
(a) to implement the investment guidelines including the
rules, policies and directions and investment mandate
in respect to the investment of funds;
(b) to reinvest the profits and proceeds of its investments
to generate further risk adjusted returns in accordance
with the investment guidelines;
(c) to make available the means to access investment
performance and activities;
(d) to prepare and submit to the Board, an annual report
within two months after the end of each financial year.
(2) A report prepared and submitted under subsection (1)(d)
must include —
(a) the investment policies applied;
(b) an explanation of the performance of each investment,
including comparison with the expectations of the Board
on the performance of the portfolio;
(c) an explanation of the manner in which the investment
policies were complied with during the financial year;
(d) a list of agents appointed by the Investment Manager;
(e) other information as the Board considers necessary.
Division 3
General
Oath of secrecy and confidentiality
36.—(1) A member of the Board or committee, Corporate Secretary,
custodian and Investment Manager shall take the prescribed oath of
secrecy.
(2) Subject to subsection (3), a member of the Board or committee,
the Corporate Secretary, custodian and Investment Manager —
(a) shall preserve the confidentiality with respect to matters
coming to his or her knowledge in the performance of his
or her duties;

67
No. 5 ] Sovereign Wealth Fund of Saint Lucia Act [ 2025
(b) shall not disclose to another person information that a
member of the Board or committee, Corporate Secretary,
custodian or Investment Manager has acquired in the
course of his or her duties or in the exercise of the
functions of the Board under this Act or any other law,
relating to —
(i) the business affairs of the Board or Fund, or
(ii) the affairs of a member of the Board or committee,
Corporate Secretary, custodian or Investment
Manager;
(c) shall not permit a person to have access to records in the
possession or control of the Board or Fund.
(3) Subsection (2) does not apply to disclosure —
(a) in respect of the affairs of a member of the Board with
the consent of the member of the Board or committee;
(b) for the purpose of enabling or assisting the Board in
exercising a function conferred on it under this Act or
any other law;
(c) if the information disclosed is or has been available to the
public from another source;
(d) if the information disclosed is in a summary or in statistics
expressed in a manner that does not enable the identity of a
member of the Board or committee, Corporate Secretary,
custodian or Investment Manager to which the information
relates, to be ascertained;
(e) lawfully made to a person with a view to the institution
of, or for the purpose of —
(i) criminal proceedings,
(ii) disciplinary proceedings relating to the discharge
of duties by a member of the Board or committee,
Corporate Secretary, Custodian or Investment
Manager, or
(iii) legal proceedings pursuant to a court order.

68
No. 5 ] Sovereign Wealth Fund of Saint Lucia Act [ 2025
(4) Where a member of the Board, Corporate Secretary,
Custodian or Investment Manager contravenes subsection (2) —
(a) in the case of a member of the Board or committee, his
or her appointment may be revoked under section 17;
(b) in the case the Corporate Secretary, custodian or Investment
Manager, his or her employment may be terminated.
Protection from liability
37.—(1) An action or other proceedings shall not lie against a
member of the Board or committee, Corporate Secretary, custodian
or Investment Manager in respect of an act done or omitted to be
done in good faith in the exercise or purported exercise of his or her
functions under this Act except in cases of personal injury.
(2) The Board shall indemnify the Corporate Secretary, custodian
or Investment Manager for the legal cost of defending an action or
other proceedings under subsection (1).
Revenue of the Board
38. The revenue of the Board comprises —
(a) sums allocated to the Board by Parliament;
(b) other sums that may become payable to or vested in the
Board in respect of matters incidental to its functions and
powers; and
(c) monies payable to the Board under another enactment.
Management of finances and application of revenue of the Board
39.—(1) Part XIII of the Public Finance Management Act, Cap.
15.01 applies to the Board in relation to finance management.
(2) The revenue of the Board in a financial year may be applied
to the payment of —
(a) remuneration payable under this Act; and
(b) expenses incurred by the Board in the discharge of its
functions under this Act.

Estimates of revenue and expenditure of the Board
40.—(1) The Board shall submit to the Minister its estimates of
revenue and expenditure in a form the Minister directs.
(2) In accordance with section 78(1)(e) of the Public Finance
Management Act, Cap. 15.01, the Board shall submit estimates of
revenue and expenditure for two subsequent financial years for the
approval of the Minister.
Strategic, financial, operational and business plan of the Board
41. In accordance with section 82 of the Public Finance
Management Act, Cap. 15.01, the Board shall submit to the Minister
—
(a) a three year strategic plan reflecting the strategic objectives
of the Board over the financial year and two subsequent
financial years; and
(b) no later than four months before the beginning of a
financial year, a financial, operational or business plan
reflecting the proposals to operationalize the strategic
objectives over the financial year.
Accounts and audit
42.—(1) In accordance with section 83 of the Public Finance
Management Act, Cap. 15.01, the Board shall make a report to the
Minister on its financial operations quarterly and at such other time
specified by the Minister in relation to its approved business plan for
the financial year.
(2) The Board shall within three months after the end of each
financial year have its accounts audited by an independent auditor
appointed by the Board who shall conduct the audit in accordance
with generally accepted international auditing standards and provide
the Board with an audited financial statement and a report on the
financial statement.
(3) A member of the Board or the Corporate Secretary shall
grant to the auditor appointed under subsection (2), access to books,
deeds, contracts, accounts, vouchers, or other documents which the
auditor considers necessary.

(4) The auditor may require a member of the Board and the
Corporate Secretary of the Board to appear, make a signed statement
or provide information in relation to the books, deeds, contracts,
accounts, vouchers, or other documents as the auditor considers
necessary.
(5) Where a member of the Board and the Corporate Secretary
contravenes subsection (3) —
(a) in the case of a member of the Board, his or her appointment
may be revoked under section 17;
(b) in the case of the Corporate Secretary, his or her

Annual report of the Board
43.—(1) The Board shall submit to the Minister, subject to subsection
(2) and not later than six months after the end of each financial year,
an annual report on the operations and activities and transactions of
the Board containing —
(a) an account of the performance of activities and
operations of the Board;
(b) an analysis of the strategic plan during the preceding
year.
(2) An annual report under subsection (1) must be accompanied
by the auditor’s report under section 42.
(3) The Minister shall submit the annual report and auditor’s
report submitted under subsection (1)(b) to be laid in Parliament within
twenty-eight days of its receipt by the Minister, or if Parliament is not
in session, within twenty-eight days of the next session of Parliament.
PART III
FINANCING OF THE FUND
Payment into the Fund
44.—(1) The resources of the Fund consists of —
(a) such funds as may be allocated by the Minister to
the Fund on the commencement of this Act including

qualifying investments that are monies of the Saint
Lucia National Economic Fund;
(b) such funds as may be acquired and earned from
investments under this Act;
(c) capital from privatization proceeds;
(d) dividends received on an investment;
(e) such other funds as may be deposited to the Fund from
any other source with the approval of the Board.
(2) In this section —
“qualifying investment” means cash paid under section 36(4)
(b) of the Citizenship by Investment Act, Cap. 1.20
“Saint Lucia National Economic Fund” means the Saint
Lucia National Economic Fund established under
section 3 of the Saint Lucia National Economic Fund
Act, Cap. 12.29.
Bank account of the Fund
45. The Board may, with the approval of the Minister, open one
or more prescribed bank accounts with a financial institution.
Payment from the Fund
46.—(1) Monies shall not be paid from the Fund except —
(a) the amount in the Fund is a total of not more than the
prescribed percentage of the gross domestic product;
(b) to meet expenditure which is chargeable under this Act;
(c) where the payment has been authorized by an
Appropriation Act under section 47.
(2) Monies shall not be paid out of the Fund except in accordance
with this Act.
(3) An Appropriation Act under subsection (1)(c) shall not be
passed if the amount in the Fund is below the amount specified under
subsection (1)(a).

(4) In this section, “expenditure” includes —

(b) meet an obligation that is directly related to the operation
of the Fund;
(c) monies for investment in accordance with the purpose of

Annual estimates
47.—(1) At least three months before the commencement of each
financial year, the Board shall cause to be prepared estimates of the
revenue and expenditure of the Fund for that financial year.
(2) The Board shall submit the estimates to the Minister.
(3) The Minister shall submit the estimates submitted under
subsection (2) to be laid in Parliament within twenty-eight days of
its receipt by the Minister, or if Parliament is not in session, within
twenty-eight days of the next session of Parliament.
(4) On approval of the estimates by Parliament, all monies
required for the purposes of this Act must be paid into the Fund.
(5) If after approval of the budget the amount appropriated for
any purpose under the Appropriation Act is insufficient or a need
has arisen for expenditure for a purpose for which no amount has
been appropriated by that Act, the Board shall prepare supplementary
estimates of revenue and expenditure in the manner specified under
subsection (2).
(6) The Minister shall submit the supplementary estimates
submitted under subsection (6) to be laid in Parliament within twenty-
eight days of its receipt by the Minister, or if Parliament is not in
session, within twenty-eight days of the next session of Parliament.

Accounts and audit of the Fund

financial year have the accounts of the Fund audited by an independent
auditor appointed by the Board, after consultation with the Director

accepted international auditing standards and provide the Board with
an audited financial statement and a report on the financial statement.

subsection (1), access to books, deeds, contracts, accounts, vouchers,

Secretary, custodian or Investment Manager to appear, make a signed

Quarterly report of the Fund
49.—(1) The Board shall no later than thirty days after the end of
each quarter submit to the Minister a quarterly report on the Fund
during the preceding quarter.
(2) A quarterly report under subsection (1) must include a report
of the inflows and outflows of the Fund, the performance of the Fund
during the quarter and the value of the assets and where the assets are

Annual report on the Fund
50.—(1) The Board shall no later than sixty days after the end of

Fund during the preceding financial year.
(2) An annual report under subsection (1) must include —
(a) a balance sheet of the Fund;

PART IV
MISCELLANEOUS
Establishment and operation of general reserve
51.—(1) The Board may establish a general reserve to which,
subject to this Act, may be appropriated from a surplus of income over
expenditure of the Fund at the end of the financial year such sums as
the Minister approves.
(2) Subject this Act, monies in the general reserve may, with
the approval of the Minister, be used for such purposes as the Board
considers expedient for the proper exercise by the Board of its functions
including the development of the assets of the Fund.
(3) The Board shall comply with any directions which the Minister
may give in relation to the management of the general reserve.
(4) Monies in the general reserve shall not be reduced, without
the approval of the Minister, below such an amount as the Minister
fixes, otherwise than for the purpose of meeting a deficiency under
subsection (5).

No. 5 ] Sovereign Wealth Fund of Saint Lucia Act [ 2025
(5) Where in a financial year the income of the Fund together
with surplus income brought forward from a previous financial year,
is insufficient to enable the Fund to meet the charges and to make the
provisions required under this Act, the deficiency shall, unless the
Minister otherwise directs, be met from the general reserve.
Prohibition from using Fund assets as collateral
52.—(1) The assets of the Fund shall not be used —
(a) to provide credit to the Government, public enterprises,
private sector entities or any person or entity;
(b) as collateral for debts, guarantees, commitments or
other liabilities of any other person or entity, whether
public or private.
(2) A contract, agreement or arrangement, to the extent that it
purports to encumber the assets under subsection (1), whether by way
of guarantee, security, mortgage or any other form of encumbrance
is null and void.
Regulations
53.—(1) The Minister, after consultation with the Board, may make
Regulations providing for all matters which by this Act are required
or permitted to be prescribed or which, in his or her opinion, are
necessary or convenient to be provided for in order to carry out or
give effect to this Act.
(2) Without limiting the generality of subsection (1) Regulations
may provide for —
(a) the general terms and conditions of service of the Corporate
Secretary, custodian or Investment Manager;
(b) a code of conduct and ethics for the Board;
